pairs.subject: supply-chain
pairs.evidence: app/api/repo-scan/route.ts:20 POST /api/repo-scan clones any github.com repository and runs a Claude CLI session with cwd set to the clone. In repo_scan mode the CLI keeps default setting sources, so the cloned repo's own project settings (including hooks, which headless -p runs do not gate behind a trust prompt) are loaded and can execute. A surface built and described as read-only therefore runs content from a stranger's tree.

techniques.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/claude_cli.py:670 Generate and web_research get --setting-sources project inside a neutral temp cwd. repo_scan gets defaults inside the cloned tree, so project-level settings and hooks from the scanned repo are honoured. There is no digest approval and no loud refusal. The heuristic walk itself reads package.json and pyproject statically, which is conformant.

pipeline/jobfit/claude_cli.py:579 The agent's tool grant is validated against a write denylist and refuses to widen. A bare Bash grant raises. The secret-file deny list is one list with three consumers (repo_scan.py:202).

pairs.registryProposal: reading-is-not-running could name agent CLIs explicitly: running a coding agent with cwd inside a cloned tree loads that tree's project settings and hooks by default, which is the 'rules that travel with the tree' sighting in its most common current form. The decision rule would be to isolate setting sources, or disable project hooks, for any agent session over a tree the operator did not write.
